newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: OSCE delegation arrives in Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: OSCE delegation arrives in Belgrade.

text.p: A delegation from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), arrived in Belgrade on Friday to investigate election fraud allegations which have sparked a month of street protests across Serbia.

The OSCE had not come to mediate but to "speak to all sides and find out the facts about the elections as quickly as possible," the head of the mission, Spain's former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, told reporters.

The OSCE mission was expected to meet leaders of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition within hours. It was still unclear whether it would meet Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic later in the day or on Saturday.

Milosevic invited the OSCE to send a delegation to Belgrade to resolve the crisis which has cost him dearly in terms of hard-won international prestige and brought fresh threats of sanctions by the United States.
Zajedno supporters and students have staged 33 days of protests over alleged vote-rigging which overturned opposition victories in 15 of Serbia's biggest towns, including the capital.

Serbian Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic said earlier on Thursday his government would not be bound by any findings made by the OSCE, saying its recommendations must be confirmed by Serbia's own institutions.
